questions.question: Obligation to seek Registration
Grant of registration & the 30-day cure
How many activities are separately registrable as CMIs under Reg 4(1)?
questions.option_A: Eleven
questions.option_B: Nine
questions.option_C: Ten
questions.option_D: Thirteen
questions.correct_text: Eleven
questions.explanation: Reg 4(1)(a)-(k) lists eleven activities: broker dealer, clearing member, credit rating agency, custodian, debenture trustee, depository participant, distributor, ERDPP, investment adviser, investment banker, and research entity.

questions.question: Since the 12 January 2026 amendment, a unit undertaking several CMI activities may:
questions.option_A: Operate without any registration if turnover is low
questions.option_B: Obtain a single unified registration for those activities
questions.option_C: Register only its highest-net-worth activity
questions.option_D: Register with the stock exchange instead of IFSCA
questions.correct_text: Obtain a single unified registration for those activities
questions.explanation: The proviso to Reg 4(1), inserted w.e.f. 12 Jan 2026, permits a unified registration for multiple activities in the manner specified by the Authority.

questions.question: What is the period of validity of a CMI certificate of registration?
questions.option_A: One year, renewable on payment of the annual fee
questions.option_B: Three years, renewable on application to the Authority
questions.option_C: Perpetual unless suspended or cancelled
questions.option_D: Five years, subject to a fresh fit-and-proper review
questions.correct_text: Perpetual unless suspended or cancelled
questions.explanation: Reg 13: the certificate granted to a CMI is perpetual unless it is suspended or cancelled by the Authority.

questions.question: In which legal forms may a CMI be present in the IFSC?
questions.option_A: Only a company incorporated in the IFSC
questions.option_B: Only a wholly-owned subsidiary
questions.option_C: Any form, including a registered partnership firm
questions.option_D: Company, LLP, body corporate, or branch thereof
questions.correct_text: Company, LLP, body corporate, or branch thereof
questions.explanation: Reg 6: a CMI must be present in the IFSC as a company, an LLP, a body corporate, or a branch thereof.

questions.question: Which step is the genuine legal defect here?
questions.option_A: Treating the certificate as unified across all activities the unit actually performs, including one it never applied for
questions.option_B: Applying through the Single Window IT System and paying the prescribed registration fees at the time of filing
questions.option_C: Submitting the application through the recognised stock exchange for a broker-dealer registration
questions.option_D: Paying the registration fees only after the Authority has communicated its satisfaction with the application
questions.correct_text: Treating the certificate as unified across all activities the unit actually performs, including one it never applied for
questions.explanation: Unified registration covers the activities applied for — not activities never included in the application. Performing an uncovered activity is unauthorised (Reg 4). SWIT filing, exchange-routing for BD, and fees-before-grant are all correct.

questions.question: What changed for multi-activity units with the 2026 amendment?
questions.option_A: Net worth requirements were removed from Schedule I altogether
questions.option_B: A unified registration option was introduced for multiple activities
questions.option_C: Registration became activity-by-activity with no consolidation
questions.option_D: Certificates became time-limited and subject to periodic renewal
questions.correct_text: A unified registration option was introduced for multiple activities
questions.explanation: Before 12 Jan 2026, a multi-activity unit collected a separate certificate per activity. The amendment inserted the unified-registration proviso to Reg 4(1).

questions.question: Two different 30-day clocks live in the registration chapter. Name them.

questions.question: Net worth requirements
Definition of 'net worth' and the liquid-assets carve-out
What is the minimum net worth for a Credit Rating Agency under Schedule I?
questions.option_D: USD 1 million
questions.explanation: Schedule I, S.No. 3: Credit Rating Agency net worth is USD 200,000.

questions.question: Following the 2026 amendment, the minimum net worth for a Custodian is:
questions.option_C: USD 1.5 million
questions.option_D: USD 1 million
questions.correct_text: USD 1 million
questions.explanation: Schedule I, S.No. 4: Custodian net worth is USD 1 million (substituted for 'as specified by the Authority' w.e.f. 12 Jan 2026). Existing custodians must comply by 30 June 2026.

questions.question: Which category carries the highest fixed net worth in Schedule I?
questions.option_A: Debenture Trustee (USD 1.5 million)
questions.option_B: Investment Banker (USD 100,000)
questions.option_C: Credit Rating Agency (USD 200,000)
questions.option_D: Custodian (USD 1 million)
questions.correct_text: Debenture Trustee (USD 1.5 million)
questions.explanation: Debenture Trustee at USD 1.5 million (Schedule I, S.No. 5) is the highest fixed figure, above Custodian's USD 1 million.

questions.concept: Net worth: at all times, highest-not-sum, branch
questions.question: A single unit is registered as a broker dealer, an investment banker and a distributor. Its net worth obligation is:
questions.option_A: The sum of the three category minimums
questions.option_B: The highest of the applicable minimums
questions.option_C: The average of the three minimums
questions.option_D: Only the distributor minimum
questions.correct_text: The highest of the applicable minimums
questions.explanation: Reg 7(4): a multi-category CMI maintains the highest of the applicable minimums, not the sum or average.

questions.question: For which set of categories does 'net worth' mean liquid assets only?
questions.option_A: All eleven categories
questions.option_B: Custodian, Debenture Trustee and Depository Participant
questions.option_C: Broker dealer, Clearing member and Investment banker
questions.option_D: Investment Adviser and Research Entity
questions.correct_text: Broker dealer, Clearing member and Investment banker
questions.explanation: Proviso to Reg 3(1)(cc): the liquid-assets definition applies to broker dealer, clearing member and investment banker.

questions.concept: Net worth: at all times, highest-not-sum, branch
questions.question: Where is the net-worth error?
questions.option_A: Measuring the broker-dealer desk's net worth on the liquid-assets basis only
questions.option_B: Earmarking the parent-level net worth specifically for the IFSC branch unit
questions.option_C: Keeping a quarterly statement of net worth as part of the eight-year records
questions.option_D: Adding the broker-dealer and investment-banker minimums together to size capital
questions.correct_text: Adding the broker-dealer and investment-banker minimums together to size capital
questions.explanation: Reg 7(4) requires the highest single minimum for a multi-category unit, not the sum. The other three steps are all correct (liquid-assets test, branch earmarking under 7(2), quarterly statement under Reg 16).

questions.question: How did Schedule I change for Custodians with the 2026 amendment?
questions.option_A: Fixed at USD 1 million (from 'as specified by the Authority')
questions.option_B: Reduced to USD 500,000 from the previous fixed figure
questions.option_C: Removed entirely, leaving it to the exchange to specify
questions.option_D: Raised to USD 1.5 million, matching the debenture trustee
questions.correct_text: Fixed at USD 1 million (from 'as specified by the Authority')
questions.explanation: The Custodian figure was substituted to USD 1 million (from 'As specified by the Authority from time to time') w.e.f. 12 Jan 2026, with existing custodians given until 30 June 2026.

questions.module_name: Fit & Proper, Principal Officer & Compliance Officer
questions.question: Reg 9(1) requires a CMI to designate:
questions.option_A: A single officer covering both roles
questions.option_B: A Principal Officer and a separate Compliance Officer, both based in the IFSC
questions.option_C: A Compliance Officer only
questions.option_D: A Principal Officer at the parent and a Compliance Officer in the IFSC
questions.correct_text: A Principal Officer and a separate Compliance Officer, both based in the IFSC
questions.explanation: Reg 9(1): a CMI shall designate a principal officer and a separate compliance officer based out of IFSC. Two distinct, IFSC-based roles.

questions.module_name: Fit & Proper, Principal Officer & Compliance Officer
questions.question: Fit-and-proper status under Reg 8 must be maintained:
questions.option_A: Only at the time of application
questions.option_B: Only for the Principal Officer
questions.option_C: At all times
questions.option_D: Only when the Authority requests confirmation
questions.correct_text: At all times
questions.explanation: Reg 8(1): the entity and its key persons must be fit and proper persons at all times.

questions.module_name: Fit & Proper, Principal Officer & Compliance Officer
questions.question: Which of these is expressly a fit-and-proper disqualification under Reg 8?
questions.option_A: Holding a passport issued by a foreign jurisdiction
questions.option_B: Operating in the IFSC as a branch of a foreign parent
questions.option_C: Advising more than one client in the same segment
questions.option_D: Being declared a fugitive economic offender
questions.correct_text: Being declared a fugitive economic offender
questions.explanation: Reg 8(2)(b) lists disqualifications including being declared a fugitive economic offender, a wilful defaulter, insolvent-and-undischarged, or convicted of moral-turpitude/economic offences.

questions.module_name: Fit & Proper, Principal Officer & Compliance Officer
questions.question: A person holding a Bachelor of Law degree is expressly eligible for appointment as:
questions.option_A: Compliance Officer
questions.option_B: Principal Officer only
questions.option_C: Controlling shareholder
questions.option_D: Neither role
questions.correct_text: Compliance Officer
questions.explanation: The second proviso to Reg 9(2) makes a Bachelor of Law holder from a recognised university eligible for appointment as a compliance officer.

questions.module_name: Fit & Proper, Principal Officer & Compliance Officer
questions.question: The graduate-plus-experience route for PO/CO qualification was amended in 2026 to require how many years of financial-services experience?
questions.option_A: Three years
questions.option_B: Five years
questions.option_C: Seven years
questions.option_D: Ten years
questions.correct_text: Five years
questions.explanation: The words 'ten' were substituted with 'five' by the 2026 amendment (w.e.f. 12 Jan 2026): a graduate now needs at least five years' financial-services experience.

questions.module_name: Fit & Proper, Principal Officer & Compliance Officer
questions.question: Identify the compliance defect.
questions.option_A: Appointing a chartered accountant as the unit's Principal Officer
questions.option_B: Basing the Compliance Officer in the IFSC rather than at the parent entity
questions.option_C: Naming the same individual as both Principal Officer and Compliance Officer
questions.option_D: Maintaining a fit-and-proper register covering directors and KMP
questions.correct_text: Naming the same individual as both Principal Officer and Compliance Officer
questions.explanation: Reg 9(1) requires a SEPARATE compliance officer — one person cannot hold both designations. A CA is qualified, IFSC-basing is required, and a fit-and-proper register is good practice.

questions.module_name: Fit & Proper, Principal Officer & Compliance Officer
questions.question: Name three categories of person to whom the fit-and-proper test applies beyond the entity itself.
Code of Conduct — all capital market intermediaries
Which regulation makes the Schedule II Code of Conduct binding on a CMI?
questions.option_A: Reg 8
questions.option_B: Reg 22
questions.option_C: Reg 41
questions.option_D: Reg 15
questions.correct_text: Reg 15
questions.explanation: Reg 15: a CMI shall abide by the Code of Conduct as specified in Schedule II.

questions.concept: Schedule II Part A — universal conduct
questions.question: Under Schedule II Part A, a CMI's duty of client confidentiality yields:
questions.option_A: Only where disclosure is required in compliance with a law in force
questions.option_B: Whenever the client's own auditors or bankers request the information
questions.option_C: Only where the CMI's board records the disclosure in its minutes
questions.option_D: Whenever disclosure would prevent a loss to another client of the firm
questions.correct_text: Only where disclosure is required in compliance with a law in force
questions.explanation: Part A cl. 8: confidentiality is maintained except where disclosure is required in compliance with any law for the time being in force.

questions.concept: Schedule II Part A — universal conduct
questions.question: The prohibition on creating a false market under Part A applies:
questions.option_A: Only to CMIs whose desks trade on their own account
questions.option_B: To a CMI acting singly or in collusion with others
questions.option_C: Only where the CMI derives a direct profit from the act
questions.option_D: Only to intermediaries dealing in listed securities
questions.correct_text: To a CMI acting singly or in collusion with others
questions.explanation: Part A cl. 5: a CMI shall not create a false market either singly or in collusion with other intermediaries or the issuer.

questions.concept: Schedule II Part A — universal conduct
questions.question: Which is the conduct breach?
questions.option_A: Declining to disclose client data to a group company absent any legal obligation
questions.option_B: Marketing the desk's genuine, evidenced track record alongside the applicable risk factors
questions.option_C: Telling a prospect the firm has 'guaranteed, unmatched returns and the best team in GIFT City'
questions.option_D: Recording a conflict of interest in the register and resolving it before acting for the client
questions.correct_text: Telling a prospect the firm has 'guaranteed, unmatched returns and the best team in GIFT City'
questions.explanation: Part A cl. 7 prohibits exaggerated statements about capability, qualification and achievement. The other actions are consistent with Part A (confidentiality cl.8, honest marketing, conflict-management cl.9).

questions.concept: Schedule II Part A — universal conduct
questions.question: Schedule II has two parts. What binds all CMIs, and what is category-specific?

questions.concept: Change in control: branch vs incorporated
questions.question: Change in control
For how long, and in what form, must a CMI preserve the records specified in Reg 16?
questions.option_A: Five years, in any form the CMI considers fit
questions.option_B: Ten years, in physical form at the registered office
questions.option_C: Three years, in electronic form only
questions.option_D: Eight years, in electronic retrieval form
questions.correct_text: Eight years, in electronic retrieval form
questions.explanation: Reg 16(1): the specified books, records and documents must be maintained in electronic retrieval form for a minimum of eight years.

questions.question: A change in a CMI's Principal Officer, Compliance Officer or KMP must be intimated to the Authority within:
questions.option_A: 15 days
questions.option_B: 7 days
questions.option_C: 30 days
questions.option_D: No fixed period
questions.correct_text: 15 days
questions.explanation: Reg 17(2): a CMI shall intimate any change in principal officer, compliance officer or KMP within 15 days.

questions.concept: Change in control: branch vs incorporated
questions.question: An IFSC-incorporated CMI facing a change in control must:
questions.option_A: Intimate the Authority within 15 days after the change
questions.option_B: Seek prior approval of the Authority before the change
questions.option_C: Only inform the market infrastructure institution
questions.option_D: Take no action unless asked
questions.correct_text: Seek prior approval of the Authority before the change
questions.explanation: Reg 23(2): an IFSC-incorporated CMI must seek prior approval of the Authority for any direct or indirect change in control. (A branch, by contrast, intimates within 15 days.)

questions.question: By when must the annual compliance audit report be furnished to the Authority?
questions.option_A: 31 March
questions.option_B: 30 June
questions.option_C: 30 September
questions.option_D: 31 December
questions.correct_text: 30 September
questions.explanation: Reg 25(2): a copy of the compliance audit report for a financial year shall be furnished to the Authority by the 30th of September of such year.

questions.question: Who may conduct a CMI's annual compliance audit under Reg 25?
questions.option_A: Any employee of the CMI who holds a recognised professional accountancy qualification
questions.option_B: Only officers of the Authority specifically deputed for the purpose
questions.option_C: The recognised stock exchange of which the intermediary is a member
questions.option_D: A member of ICAI, ICSI or ICMAI, or a person authorised to audit in a Foreign Jurisdiction
questions.correct_text: A member of ICAI, ICSI or ICMAI, or a person authorised to audit in a Foreign Jurisdiction
questions.explanation: Reg 25(1): the audit is conducted by a member of ICAI, ICSI or ICMAI, or a person authorised to conduct audit in a Foreign Jurisdiction.

questions.concept: Change in control: branch vs incorporated
questions.question: Spot the resilience/governance lapse.
questions.option_A: An IFSC-incorporated CMI closing a change of control and then intimating IFSCA 15 days later
questions.option_B: Reviewing the business continuity plan annually and upon any material change to systems
questions.option_C: Preserving the specified records in electronic retrieval form for a full eight years
questions.option_D: Filing the annual compliance audit report with the Authority by the 30th of September
questions.correct_text: An IFSC-incorporated CMI closing a change of control and then intimating IFSCA 15 days later
questions.explanation: Reg 23(2) requires an incorporated CMI to obtain PRIOR approval for a change in control — post-closing intimation is the branch rule (23(1)), not the incorporated rule. The other three are correct.

questions.question: On the resilience stack, which is a Reg 20 requirement specifically?
questions.option_A: A cyber security and cyber resilience framework
questions.option_B: A business continuity plan, reviewed annually
questions.option_C: An arm's-length policy for research
questions.option_D: A rating monitoring process
questions.correct_text: A business continuity plan, reviewed annually
questions.explanation: Reg 20: maintain a BCP, updated on material change and reviewed annually. Cyber is Reg 21; the others are category-specific.

questions.question: Name two records Reg 16 expressly requires beyond the basic financial statements.
Suspension, cancellation or other actions
Under Reg 37, the Authority may order an inspection:
questions.option_A: Only after a direction issued by a court or tribunal
questions.option_B: Only once in each financial year, on prior written notice
questions.option_C: Suo motu or upon receipt of information or a complaint
questions.option_D: Only with the written consent of the intermediary concerned
questions.correct_text: Suo motu or upon receipt of information or a complaint
questions.explanation: Reg 37(1): the Authority may, suo motu or upon receipt of information or complaint, at any time appoint an inspecting authority.

questions.question: Which is expressly a standalone ground for action under Reg 41?
questions.option_A: Reporting an operating loss for two consecutive financial years despite adequate net worth
questions.option_B: Operating more than one registered activity from a single unit without separate premises
questions.option_C: Being structured as a branch of a foreign parent rather than incorporated in the IFSC
questions.option_D: Furnishing information to the Authority that is false or misleading in any material particular
questions.correct_text: Furnishing information to the Authority that is false or misleading in any material particular
questions.explanation: Reg 41(1)(d): furnishing false or misleading information in any material particular is its own ground for suspension/cancellation.

questions.question: For broker dealers, clearing members and depository participants, who else may inspect or suspend them besides IFSCA?
questions.option_A: The recognised stock exchange, clearing corporation or depository respectively, under its bye-laws
questions.option_B: No other body at all; supervision of registered intermediaries rests solely with the Authority
questions.option_C: The Ministry of Finance, in cases where the intermediary handles foreign-currency business
questions.option_D: The intermediary's statutory auditors, in the course of the annual compliance audit report
questions.correct_text: The recognised stock exchange, clearing corporation or depository respectively, under its bye-laws
questions.explanation: Reg 37(4) and Reg 41(2)-(4): the recognised stock exchange, clearing corporation or depository may inspect/suspend a BD, CM or DP respectively under applicable laws — a dual-oversight layer.

questions.question: An application for relaxation of strict enforcement under Reg 44 is:
questions.option_A: Granted automatically on filing, subject to later review
questions.option_B: Accompanied by a non-refundable fee and processed within 30 days
questions.option_C: Available only to recognised exchanges and clearing corporations
questions.option_D: Available as of right to every registered intermediary on request
questions.correct_text: Accompanied by a non-refundable fee and processed within 30 days
questions.explanation: Reg 44: relaxation is sought by application with a non-refundable fee; the Authority processes it within 30 days of a complete application and records reasons.

questions.question: Which response to an inspection is itself a Reg 41 ground for action?
questions.option_A: Producing the eight-year electronic records promptly on the inspecting authority's request
questions.option_B: Giving the inspecting authority a full and accurate reply within the time allowed
questions.option_C: Declining to co-operate with the inspection until 'legal review' concludes indefinitely
questions.option_D: Resolving the investor complaint that prompted the inspection and recording the outcome
questions.correct_text: Declining to co-operate with the inspection until 'legal review' concludes indefinitely
questions.explanation: Reg 41(1)(f): failure to co-operate in any enquiry, inspection or investigation is a standalone ground — independent of the underlying issue. The other responses are all compliant.

questions.question: What did Reg 47 do on commencement of the 2025 Regulations?
questions.option_A: Introduced unified registration for multi-activity units in the IFSC
questions.option_B: Abolished the net worth requirements prescribed under Schedule I
questions.option_C: Created the ESG Ratings and Data Products Provider category
questions.option_D: Repealed the IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2021
questions.correct_text: Repealed the IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2021
questions.explanation: Reg 47(1): on and from commencement, the IFSCA (CMI) Regulations, 2021 stand repealed (with a saving for Chapter V of the 2021 regs on foreign-jurisdiction dealing until Reg 27 norms are specified).

questions.question: Must the Authority always give notice before inspecting a CMI?
Cross-permissions without separate registration
A broker dealer's minimum net worth is:
questions.option_A: As specified by the recognised stock exchange
questions.option_B: USD 100,000 fixed under Schedule I
questions.option_C: As specified by the recognised clearing corporation
questions.option_D: USD 200,000, matching the rating-agency floor
questions.correct_text: As specified by the recognised stock exchange
questions.explanation: Schedule I, S.No. 1: broker dealer (trading member) net worth is as specified by the recognised stock exchange.

questions.question: For a clearing member, 'net worth' is defined as:
questions.option_A: Ordinary balance-sheet net worth as defined generally
questions.option_B: The aggregate value of liquid assets
questions.option_C: Paid-up share capital and free reserves only
questions.option_D: Net worth computed on a turnover-linked basis
questions.correct_text: The aggregate value of liquid assets
questions.explanation: Proviso to Reg 3(1)(cc): for a broker dealer, clearing member or investment banker, net worth means the aggregate value of liquid assets.

questions.question: A registered clearing member wishes to also act as a broker dealer on the same exchange. It must:
questions.option_A: Obtain a fresh certificate of registration from the Authority for the broking role
questions.option_B: Incorporate a separate legal entity in the IFSC to carry on the broking activity
questions.option_C: Obtain the recognised stock exchange's approval; no separate certificate is required
questions.option_D: Do nothing; the clearing-member certificate covers broker-dealing automatically
questions.correct_text: Obtain the recognised stock exchange's approval; no separate certificate is required
questions.explanation: Reg 5(4)(a): with the recognised stock exchange's approval, a clearing member may act as a broker dealer without a separate certificate of registration.

questions.question: Which is the misstep?
questions.option_A: Following the recognised stock exchange's bye-laws as the operating rulebook for the trading desk
questions.option_B: Measuring the broker-dealer desk's net worth on a liquid-assets basis rather than the balance sheet
questions.option_C: Tracking the exchange-specified net-worth figure and reviewing it at the end of each quarter
questions.option_D: Assuming exchange approval to act as clearing member also authorises a new fund-distribution business
questions.correct_text: Assuming exchange approval to act as clearing member also authorises a new fund-distribution business
questions.explanation: Reg 5(4)-(5) cover BD/CM role-crossing only. Distribution is a separate registrable activity (Reg 4) needing its own registration — MII approval doesn't extend to it.

questions.question: Which three categories share the liquid-assets net-worth definition?
Continuous monitoring and constrained withdrawal
A Credit Rating Agency's minimum net worth is:
questions.option_D: USD 1 million
questions.explanation: Schedule I, S.No. 3: USD 200,000.

questions.question: Under Reg 28(1), before rating a client's securities a CRA must:
questions.option_A: Obtain the prior approval of the recognised stock exchange concerned
questions.option_B: Enter into a written agreement setting out rights, liabilities and fees
questions.option_C: Publish an indicative rating and invite comments from the issuer
questions.option_D: Deposit the prescribed sum with the Authority before publishing
questions.correct_text: Enter into a written agreement setting out rights, liabilities and fees
questions.explanation: Reg 28(1): a CRA shall enter into a written agreement with each client, including the rights, liabilities and fee.

questions.question: A CRA should generally NOT withdraw a rating when:
questions.option_A: The client requests withdrawal for its own commercial convenience
questions.option_B: A periodic review of the rating has fallen due under its policy
questions.option_C: The obligations under the rated instrument are still outstanding
questions.option_D: The rating fee for the current year has been paid in full
questions.correct_text: The obligations under the rated instrument are still outstanding
questions.explanation: Reg 28(5): a CRA shall generally not withdraw a rating so long as the obligations under the rated security/instrument/facility are outstanding (save specified exceptions).

questions.question: Identify the CRA lapse.
questions.option_A: Documenting the rating relationship in a written agreement covering rights, liabilities and fees
questions.option_B: Continuously monitoring outstanding ratings and recording the outcome of each periodic review
questions.option_C: Carrying out periodic reviews of every live rating in line with its published rating policy
questions.option_D: Withdrawing a rating on a live instrument simply because the client asked, with no permitted trigger
questions.correct_text: Withdrawing a rating on a live instrument simply because the client asked, with no permitted trigger
questions.explanation: Reg 28(5): withdrawal while obligations are outstanding is constrained to specified situations — a bare client request is not one. The other steps comply with Reg 28.

questions.question: Does the liquid-assets net-worth definition apply to a CRA?
Segregation of custodian activities
Following the 2026 amendment, a custodian's minimum net worth is:
questions.option_A: USD 1 million
questions.option_D: USD 1.5 million
questions.correct_text: USD 1 million
questions.explanation: Schedule I, S.No. 4: USD 1 million (substituted w.e.f. 12 Jan 2026).

questions.question: By when must a custodian already registered before the amendment meet the revised net worth?
questions.option_A: 1 October 2025
questions.option_B: 30 June 2026
questions.option_C: 31 March 2026
questions.option_D: 31 December 2026
questions.correct_text: 30 June 2026
questions.explanation: Schedule I, S.No. 4: existing custodians required to infuse or earmark additional funds under the revised norms comply by 30 June 2026.

questions.question: The cardinal operating duty of a custodian under Reg 29(1) is to:
questions.option_A: Rate the securities held in custody for its clients
questions.option_B: Guarantee the returns earned on custodied assets
questions.option_C: Separate and segregate custody from all other activities
questions.option_D: Advise clients on which securities they should buy
questions.correct_text: Separate and segregate custody from all other activities
questions.explanation: Reg 29(1): a custodian shall separate and segregate its custodian activities from all other activities.

questions.question: Where is the custodian control failure?
questions.option_A: Documenting the custody terms agreed with each client in a written agreement before onboarding them
questions.option_B: Running periodic reconciliations of the assets held in custody for every individual client account
questions.option_C: Protecting the custody records from manipulation, from theft and from natural hazard alike
questions.option_D: Operating the custody desk on the same books and access profile as the proprietary trading desk 'for efficiency'
questions.correct_text: Operating the custody desk on the same books and access profile as the proprietary trading desk 'for efficiency'
questions.explanation: Reg 29(1) requires custody to be separated and segregated from all other activities — sharing books/access with a trading desk defeats segregation. The other steps comply with Reg 29(3)-(4).

questions.concept: Debenture trustee: independence, reporting, nominee director
questions.question: A debenture trustee's minimum net worth is:
questions.option_A: USD 1.5 million
questions.option_C: USD 1 million
questions.option_D: As specified by the depository
questions.correct_text: USD 1.5 million
questions.explanation: Schedule I, S.No. 5: USD 1.5 million — the highest fixed figure in Schedule I.

questions.concept: Debenture trustee: independence, reporting, nominee director
questions.question: A debenture trustee's appointment is barred where it:
questions.option_A: Holds net worth of USD 1.5 million rather than a higher amount
questions.option_B: Is an associate of the issuer or likely to have a conflict of interest
questions.option_C: Operates in the IFSC as a branch rather than an incorporated entity
questions.option_D: Reports to debenture holders quarterly rather than half-yearly
questions.correct_text: Is an associate of the issuer or likely to have a conflict of interest
questions.explanation: Reg 30(2): a person shall not be appointed debenture trustee where it is an associate of the issuer or is likely to have a conflict of interest.

questions.concept: Debenture trustee: independence, reporting, nominee director
questions.question: The debenture trustee must appoint a nominee director on the issuer's board on:
questions.option_A: Any single late payment of interest on the rated debentures, however brief the delay
questions.option_B: A written request from the issuer's board seeking trustee representation on it
questions.option_C: Two consecutive defaults in interest, or default in security creation or redemption
questions.option_D: A sustained fall in the market price of the debentures below their par value
questions.correct_text: Two consecutive defaults in interest, or default in security creation or redemption
questions.explanation: Reg 30(3)(f): the nominee-director trigger is two consecutive interest defaults, or default in creation of security, or default in redemption.

questions.concept: Debenture trustee: independence, reporting, nominee director
questions.question: The debenture trustee's periodic reports from the issuer are called for within:
questions.option_A: Thirty days of the end of the relevant quarter, irrespective of any board meetings
questions.option_B: Fifteen days of the board meeting or 60 days of the quarter, whichever is later
questions.option_C: Ninety days of the end of the issuer's financial year, with the annual report
questions.option_D: Seven days of the relevant board meeting or 45 days of the quarter, whichever is earlier
questions.correct_text: Seven days of the relevant board meeting or 45 days of the quarter, whichever is earlier
questions.explanation: Reg 30(3)(c): within seven days of the relevant board meeting or within forty-five days of the respective quarter, whichever is earlier.

questions.concept: Debenture trustee: independence, reporting, nominee director
questions.question: Spot the debenture-trustee failure.
questions.option_A: Waiting for three or four missed interest payments before acting, treating 'two consecutive' as merely indicative
questions.option_B: Signing the trust deed with the issuer well before the subscription list for the issue opens to the public
questions.option_C: Declining the appointment on discovering that it is an associate of the issuer of these debentures
questions.option_D: Calling for utilisation-of-funds reports from the issuer within each of the periods prescribed by regulation
questions.correct_text: Waiting for three or four missed interest payments before acting, treating 'two consecutive' as merely indicative
questions.explanation: Reg 30(3)(f) sets 'two consecutive defaults in interest' as the trigger — it is a bright line, not indicative. Delaying escalation past it fails debenture holders. The other steps comply with Reg 30.

questions.concept: Debenture trustee: independence, reporting, nominee director
questions.question: When must the debenture-trustee/issuer agreement be in place?
Beneficial-owner segregation and daily reconciliation
A depository participant's minimum net worth is:
questions.option_B: As specified by the depository
questions.option_D: As specified by the clearing corporation
questions.correct_text: As specified by the depository
questions.explanation: Schedule I, S.No. 6: as specified by the depository.

questions.question: How often must a depository participant reconcile its records with the depository?
questions.option_A: Monthly
questions.option_B: Weekly
questions.option_C: Daily
questions.option_D: Quarterly
questions.correct_text: Daily
questions.explanation: Reg 31(5): a DP shall reconcile its records with the depository on a daily basis.

questions.question: Under Reg 31(2), a beneficial owner's securities:
questions.option_A: May be pooled with other beneficial owners' holdings for operational efficiency
questions.option_B: May be lent out at the depository participant's discretion to other clients
questions.option_C: Are held within the depository participant's own proprietary account
questions.option_D: Must be segregated and not mixed with other owners' or the DP's own securities
questions.correct_text: Must be segregated and not mixed with other owners' or the DP's own securities
questions.explanation: Reg 31(2): separate accounts per beneficial owner, with securities segregated and never commingled.

questions.question: Identify the DP breach.
questions.option_A: Holding a small buffer of client securities in the DP's own proprietary account 'for operational ease'
questions.option_B: Opening and maintaining a separate account in the name of each beneficial owner as required
questions.option_C: Reconciling its own records with those of the depository at the close of every business day
questions.option_D: Maintaining data-processing integrity across all of its electronic records
questions.correct_text: Holding a small buffer of client securities in the DP's own proprietary account 'for operational ease'
questions.explanation: Reg 31(2) forbids mixing beneficial owners' securities with the participant's own securities. The other steps comply with Reg 31.

questions.question: Does a depository participant use the liquid-assets net-worth definition?
Permitted distribution activities
A distributor's minimum net worth is:
questions.explanation: Schedule I, S.No. 7: USD 50,000.

questions.question: Under the distributor's Part B code, attracting clients through an offer of rebate is:
questions.option_A: Permitted if disclosed
questions.option_B: Permitted for sophisticated investors
questions.option_C: Expressly to be abstained from
questions.option_D: Required for fairness
questions.correct_text: Expressly to be abstained from
questions.explanation: Schedule II Part B (distributor): a registered distributor shall abstain from attracting clients through offer of rebate.

questions.question: Distribution to sophisticated investors under Reg 32(1) is:
questions.option_A: Prohibited entirely, because sophisticated investors are separately regulated elsewhere
questions.option_B: Limited to capital market products domiciled in the IFSC and nowhere else at all
questions.option_C: Allowed only with the prior approval of the recognised stock exchange concerned
questions.option_D: Wider — products from issuers/providers set up in India, IFSC or any foreign jurisdiction
questions.correct_text: Wider — products from issuers/providers set up in India, IFSC or any foreign jurisdiction
questions.explanation: Reg 32(1)(b): distribution to sophisticated investors covers products offered by any issuer/service provider set up in India, IFSC or any foreign jurisdiction — broader than the ordinary-client channel.

questions.question: Spot the distributor conduct breach.
questions.option_A: Offering a cash rebate to attract new retail clients
questions.option_B: Classifying clients before recommending products
questions.option_C: Disclosing all material information to prospective clients
questions.option_D: Segregating proprietary investments from client distribution
questions.correct_text: Offering a cash rebate to attract new retail clients
questions.explanation: The distributor Part B code prohibits attracting clients through rebate. The other steps are consistent with the distributor's duties.

questions.question: Which Gazette notification anchors the 'specified jurisdictions' for certain distribution channels?
ERDPP comply-or-explain code and disclosure
An ERDPP's minimum net worth is:
questions.explanation: Schedule I, S.No. 8: USD 25,000.

questions.question: The ERDPP code of conduct is applied on what basis?
questions.option_A: Strict liability
questions.option_B: Voluntary only
questions.option_C: 'Comply or explain'
questions.option_D: Exchange-approved
questions.correct_text: 'Comply or explain'
questions.explanation: Reg 33(3): the ERDPP adheres to its code of conduct on a 'comply' or 'explain' basis.

questions.question: An ERDPP is best described as:
questions.option_A: A specialised type of credit rating agency under Reg 28
questions.option_B: A distributor of ESG-themed funds and products to IFSC clients
questions.option_C: A depository participant offering ESG data services
questions.option_D: A separate category dealing in ESG ratings and data products
questions.correct_text: A separate category dealing in ESG ratings and data products
questions.explanation: The ERDPP is its own Reg 4(1)(h) category for ESG ratings and data products — distinct from a credit rating agency.

questions.question: Spot the category error.
questions.option_A: Applying CRA-style continuous-monitoring-and-withdrawal rules to ESG ratings because 'a rating is a rating'
questions.option_B: Publishing a comply-or-explain disclosure setting out precisely how it has complied with its code
questions.option_C: Recording the reasoning behind each departure from the code that it has chosen to explain
questions.option_D: Maintaining net worth of USD 25,000 as Schedule I requires of an ERDPP
questions.correct_text: Applying CRA-style continuous-monitoring-and-withdrawal rules to ESG ratings because 'a rating is a rating'
questions.explanation: CRA duties under Reg 28 do not govern an ERDPP; the ERDPP has its own comply-or-explain code under Reg 33. The other steps are correct for an ERDPP.

questions.question: Which three categories all share a USD 25,000 net worth?
Fee-only advice and the 15-day own-account restriction
An investment adviser may receive remuneration:
questions.option_A: From product manufacturers as commission on the schemes recommended
questions.option_B: Only from the client being advised, for the underlying products
questions.option_C: From any counterparty to the transaction, if disclosed to the client
questions.option_D: From the recognised stock exchange on which the product is traded
questions.correct_text: Only from the client being advised, for the underlying products
questions.explanation: Reg 34(4): an IA shall not receive consideration from any person other than the client being advised, in respect of the underlying products.

questions.question: An investment adviser must not trade on its own account contrary to its advice for:
questions.option_A: 24 hours
questions.option_B: 7 days
questions.option_C: 15 days
questions.option_D: 30 days
questions.correct_text: 15 days
questions.explanation: Reg 34(6): no own-account transaction contrary to advice for 15 days from the advice (with a 24-hour revised-assessment exception).

questions.question: Towards its clients, an investment adviser acts in:
questions.option_A: A best-efforts capacity, subject to the client's own judgement
questions.option_B: A purely execution capacity, acting on client instructions only
questions.option_C: A commission-agent capacity, owing duties to the product provider
questions.option_D: A fiduciary capacity, disclosing conflicts as they arise
questions.correct_text: A fiduciary capacity, disclosing conflicts as they arise
questions.explanation: Reg 34(3): an IA acts in a fiduciary capacity and discloses all conflicts of interest as and when they arise.

questions.question: Which arrangement breaches the adviser rules?
questions.option_A: Accepting a trail commission from the fund house whose scheme it recommends
questions.option_B: Charging the client a flat advisory fee agreed in the engagement letter
questions.option_C: Disclosing a personal holding in a security it has recommended to clients
questions.option_D: Maintaining arm's-length separation between advisory and other activities
questions.correct_text: Accepting a trail commission from the fund house whose scheme it recommends
questions.explanation: Reg 34(4) bars any remuneration from a person other than the advised client for the underlying products — a fund-house trail commission is exactly that. The other steps comply with Reg 34.

questions.question: What is the exception to the adviser's 15-day own-account restriction?
Promoter/associate conflict limit
An investment banker's minimum net worth is:
questions.explanation: Schedule I, S.No. 10: USD 100,000.

questions.question: For an investment banker, net worth is measured as:
questions.option_A: Ordinary balance-sheet net worth
questions.option_B: Paid-up capital only
questions.option_C: The aggregate value of liquid assets
questions.option_D: Turnover-based
questions.correct_text: The aggregate value of liquid assets
questions.explanation: Proviso to Reg 3(1)(cc): for an investment banker (as for a broker dealer and clearing member), net worth means the aggregate value of liquid assets.

questions.question: Where an investment banker is a promoter or associate of the issuer, it may:
questions.option_A: Act as sole book-running lead manager
questions.option_B: Do anything, if it discloses the relationship
questions.option_C: Rate the issue
questions.option_D: Undertake only marketing of the issue or offer
questions.correct_text: Undertake only marketing of the issue or offer
questions.explanation: Reg 35(3): a promoter/associate IB shall not undertake any activity except marketing of the issue or offer.

questions.question: Spot the investment-banker breach.
questions.option_A: Acting as book-running lead manager for an issue by a company of which it is a promoter
questions.option_B: Documenting the issue-management mandate with the issuer before work begins
questions.option_C: Demarcating responsibilities clearly among the several joint lead bankers
questions.option_D: Computing its net worth on the liquid-assets basis rather than the balance sheet
questions.correct_text: Acting as book-running lead manager for an issue by a company of which it is a promoter
questions.explanation: Reg 35(3) confines a promoter/associate IB to marketing only — book-running for an issuer it promotes is prohibited. The other steps comply with Reg 35 and Reg 3(1)(cc).

questions.question: What is the defining activity of an 'investment banker' under these regulations?
Research-entity registration exemption
A research entity's minimum net worth is:
questions.explanation: Schedule I, S.No. 11: USD 25,000.

questions.question: Under Reg 4(4), who is exempt from separate registration as a research entity?
questions.option_A: Any person who issues research reports without charging a separate fee
questions.option_B: Only entities incorporated outside the IFSC and regulated in their home state
questions.option_C: A registered IA, CRA or FME that issues research reports to the public
questions.option_D: No person; every research provider must obtain a separate registration
questions.correct_text: A registered IA, CRA or FME that issues research reports to the public
questions.explanation: Reg 4(4): a registered investment adviser, credit rating agency or Fund Management Entity issuing/circulating/distributing research reports to the public need not separately register as a research entity.

questions.question: A research entity's core structural duty under Reg 36(4) is to:
questions.option_A: Guarantee the accuracy of every research recommendation it publishes
questions.option_B: Rate the securities it researches using a published rating scale
questions.option_C: Distribute research only to sophisticated investors in the IFSC
questions.option_D: Ensure the independence of research from its other business activities
questions.correct_text: Ensure the independence of research from its other business activities
questions.explanation: Reg 36(4): a research entity shall have appropriate mechanisms to ensure the independence of its research activities from its other business activities.

questions.question: Identify the research-entity control gap.
questions.option_A: Letting analysts trade the securities they cover on an honour system with no monitoring
questions.option_B: Maintaining written policies that govern analyst dealing and personal trading accounts
questions.option_C: Monitoring and recording analyst personal trading against the firm's restricted list
questions.option_D: Ring-fencing the research function from the firm's other business and reporting lines
questions.correct_text: Letting analysts trade the securities they cover on an honour system with no monitoring
questions.explanation: Reg 36(5)-(6) require analyst personal trading to be monitored, recorded and, where necessary, formally approved — an honour system with no monitoring fails this. The other steps comply with Reg 36.

questions.question: A standalone firm that only issues public research and holds no other IFSCA registration — does it need to register?
Which of these is a COMMON obligation binding every CMI?
questions.option_A: Reconciling records with the depository daily
questions.option_B: Maintaining the Schedule II Part A code of conduct
questions.option_C: Acting in a fiduciary capacity and receiving no third-party remuneration
questions.option_D: Appointing a nominee director on two consecutive interest defaults
questions.correct_text: Maintaining the Schedule II Part A code of conduct
questions.explanation: Schedule II Part A (via Reg 15) binds all CMIs. Daily reconciliation is DP-specific (Reg 31), fiduciary/fee-only is IA-specific (Reg 34), and the nominee director is DT-specific (Reg 30).

questions.question: Which obligation is ENTITY-SPECIFIC, not common?
questions.option_A: Maintaining net worth at all times
questions.option_B: Furnishing a quarterly statement of net worth
questions.option_C: Measuring net worth as liquid assets only
questions.option_D: Undergoing an annual compliance audit
questions.correct_text: Measuring net worth as liquid assets only
questions.explanation: The liquid-assets definition applies only to broker dealers, clearing members and investment bankers (Reg 3(1)(cc)). The other three are common: at-all-times maintenance (Reg 7), quarterly statement (Reg 16), and annual audit (Reg 25).

questions.question: A multi-desk unit (broker dealer + investment banker + distributor) asks what net worth it must hold. The correct answer is:
questions.option_A: The sum of the three Schedule I minimums
questions.option_B: Only the distributor's USD 50,000
questions.option_C: The average of the three
questions.option_D: The highest of the applicable minimums
questions.correct_text: The highest of the applicable minimums
questions.explanation: Reg 7(4): a multi-category CMI holds the highest of the applicable minimums. Here the BD/IB figures apply on a liquid-assets basis; the single highest applicable minimum governs — not the sum.

questions.question: Meridian Capital (BD + IB + distributor desks; group custody desk) makes four compliance calls. Which is WRONG?
questions.option_A: Treats the IA fee-only rule as binding on its distributor desk
questions.option_B: Applies Schedule II Part A conduct across all of its desks
questions.option_C: Runs the group custody desk segregated from the other desks
questions.option_D: Computes its net worth on the highest-of basis, not the sum
questions.correct_text: Treats the IA fee-only rule as binding on its distributor desk
questions.explanation: The fee-only rule (Reg 34(4)) is investment-ADVISER-specific; it does not bind a distributor, which may be product-remunerated. Meridian has no IA desk here. The other three calls are correct.

questions.question: Which duty is COMMON to all CMIs?
questions.option_A: Segregating custody from other activities
questions.option_B: Seeking prior approval / intimating a change in control
questions.option_C: Entering a written agreement before rating securities
questions.option_D: Appointing a nominee director on default
questions.correct_text: Seeking prior approval / intimating a change in control
questions.explanation: Change-in-control (Reg 23) binds every CMI (branch intimates; incorporated seeks prior approval). Custody segregation (Reg 29), the CRA rating agreement (Reg 28) and the DT nominee director (Reg 30) are each category-specific.

questions.question: The '15-day' rule that is ENTITY-SPECIFIC to investment advisers is:
questions.option_A: 15 days to intimate a change in Compliance Officer
questions.option_B: The applicant's 15-day deficiency-cure window
questions.option_C: No own-account trading contrary to advice for 15 days
questions.option_D: 15 days for the exchange to forward its recommendation
questions.correct_text: No own-account trading contrary to advice for 15 days
questions.explanation: Reg 34(6)'s 15-day own-account restriction is IA-specific. The PO/CO-change intimation (Reg 17(2), 15 days) is common; there is no 15-day cure (it is 30 days, Reg 12); and the exchange forwarding clock is 30 days (Reg 5(2)).

questions.question: Across the 2026 amendments, which change was COMMON (affecting registration for all), rather than a single category's figure?
questions.option_A: Custodian net worth being fixed at USD 1 million in Schedule I
questions.option_B: The USD 25,000 tier applying to ERDPP, IA and research entities
questions.option_C: Debenture trustee net worth remaining at USD 1.5 million
questions.option_D: Introduction of unified registration for multi-activity units
questions.correct_text: Introduction of unified registration for multi-activity units
questions.explanation: Unified registration (proviso to Reg 4(1)) is a common, cross-category registration change. The others are category-specific Schedule I figures.

questions.question: Give the one-line method for classifying any CMI obligation.
There are 13 separately registrable activities under Reg 4(1).
questions.explanation: Reg 4(1) runs from (a) to (k) — eleven activities, not thirteen.

questions.question: A unified registration means a multi-activity unit only has to comply with one set of category obligations.
questions.explanation: Unified registration consolidates the certificate, not the compliance. Each activity keeps its Chapter IV obligations and its Part B conduct code.

questions.question: Reg 4(1)(a)–(k) lists ___ separately registrable activities.
questions.explanation: Eleven — the clause letters run A to K.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a registrable activity under Reg 4(1)?
questions.option_A: Portfolio Manager
questions.option_B: Debenture Trustee
questions.option_C: Custodian
questions.option_D: ESG Ratings and Data Products Provider
questions.correct_text: Portfolio Manager
questions.explanation: Reg 4(1) lists broker dealer, clearing member, credit rating agency, custodian, debenture trustee, depository participant, distributor, ERDPP, investment adviser, investment banker and research entity. 'Portfolio Manager' is not among them.

questions.question: An applicant given a deficiency letter has ___ days to rectify before registration may be refused.
questions.explanation: Reg 12(2): thirty days to cure. Distinct from Reg 5(2)'s thirty-day exchange-forwarding clock.

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes the two 30-day clocks in the registration chapter?
questions.option_A: Both run against the applicant
questions.option_B: Reg 5(2) binds the exchange/CC/depository to forward its recommendation; Reg 12(2) gives the applicant time to cure deficiencies
questions.option_C: Reg 5(2) is the cure period and Reg 12(2) is the forwarding period
questions.option_D: Only one 30-day clock exists
questions.correct_text: Reg 5(2) binds the exchange/CC/depository to forward its recommendation; Reg 12(2) gives the applicant time to cure deficiencies
questions.explanation: Two different parties, two different triggers, same duration — a classic confusion.

questions.question: A CMI certificate of registration must be renewed every five years.
questions.explanation: Reg 13: the certificate is perpetual unless suspended or cancelled. There is no renewal cycle.

questions.question: Surrender of registration takes effect the moment the CMI files its application.
questions.explanation: Reg 14: voluntary surrender is effective only once the Authority accepts it.

questions.question: Credit Rating Agency minimum net worth: USD ___
questions.explanation: Schedule I, S.No. 3.

questions.question: Custodian minimum net worth (2026 amendment): USD ___
questions.explanation: Schedule I, S.No. 4 — substituted w.e.f. 12 Jan 2026; existing custodians comply by 30 June 2026.

questions.question: Debenture Trustee minimum net worth: USD ___
questions.explanation: Schedule I, S.No. 5 — the highest fixed figure in the Schedule.

questions.question: Investment Banker minimum net worth: USD ___
questions.explanation: Schedule I, S.No. 10 — measured on liquid assets.

questions.question: Distributor minimum net worth: USD ___
questions.explanation: Schedule I, S.No. 7.

questions.question: Existing custodians must meet the revised net worth by 30 ___ 2026.
questions.explanation: Schedule I, S.No. 4.

questions.question: Which category does NOT use the ordinary balance-sheet net-worth definition?
questions.option_A: Credit Rating Agency
questions.option_B: Custodian
questions.option_C: Clearing member
questions.option_D: Debenture Trustee
questions.correct_text: Clearing member
questions.explanation: Proviso to Reg 3(1)(cc): only broker dealer, clearing member and investment banker measure net worth as liquid assets.

questions.concept: Net worth: at all times, highest-not-sum, branch
questions.question: A CMI registered in three categories must hold the sum of the three minimum net worth figures.
questions.explanation: Reg 7(4): the highest of the applicable minimums, not the sum.

questions.question: Schedule I prescribes both a net worth and a deposit for each category.
questions.explanation: Schedule I is net worth only. There is no deposit requirement anywhere in the CMI Regulations.

questions.concept: Net worth: at all times, highest-not-sum, branch
questions.question: Complete the statement: net worth under Reg 7(1) must be …
questions.option_A: met on the date of application
questions.option_B: tested annually at year end
questions.option_C: certified once every three years
questions.option_D: maintained at all times
questions.correct_text: maintained at all times
questions.explanation: Reg 7(1): maintained at all times — a continuing test, evidenced by the quarterly net-worth statement under Reg 16.

questions.question: Match each category to its Schedule I minimum net worth.
questions.explanation: Schedule I, S.Nos. 3, 10, 5 and 9 respectively.
questions.pairs: Credit Rating Agency = USD 200,000 ; Investment Banker = USD 100,000 ; Debenture Trustee = USD 1.5 million ; Investment Adviser = USD 25,000

questions.question: One suitably qualified person may serve as both Principal Officer and Compliance Officer.
questions.explanation: Reg 9(1) requires a principal officer AND a separate compliance officer, both based out of IFSC.

questions.question: A graduate needs at least ___ years' financial-services experience to qualify as PO or CO (2026 amendment).
questions.explanation: Reg 9(2) proviso — 'ten' substituted with 'five' w.e.f. 12 Jan 2026.

questions.question: Fit and proper status is tested only at the time of application.
questions.explanation: Reg 8(1): the entity and its key persons must be fit and proper at all times.

questions.question: Which is NOT among the persons to whom the fit-and-proper test applies?
questions.option_A: Every employee of the CMI
questions.option_B: Controlling shareholders
questions.option_C: Key managerial personnel
questions.option_D: Directors or designated partners
questions.correct_text: Every employee of the CMI
questions.explanation: Reg 8(1) reaches the entity, its principal officer, directors/designated partners, KMP and controlling shareholders — not the entire workforce.

questions.concept: Schedule II Part A — universal conduct
questions.question: Client confidentiality under Schedule II Part A yields whenever disclosure is commercially convenient.
questions.explanation: Part A cl. 8: confidentiality yields only where disclosure is required in compliance with a law in force.

questions.concept: Schedule II Part A — universal conduct
questions.question: A CMI is prohibited from creating a false market …
questions.option_A: only when acting alone
questions.option_B: whether acting singly or in collusion with others
questions.option_C: only when it profits directly
questions.option_D: only if it is a broker dealer
questions.correct_text: whether acting singly or in collusion with others
questions.explanation: Part A cl. 5 — singly or in collusion with other intermediaries or the issuer.

questions.question: Records under Reg 16 must be preserved for a minimum of ___ years.
questions.explanation: Reg 16(1) — in electronic retrieval form.

questions.question: A change in PO, CO or KMP must be intimated within ___ days.
The annual compliance audit report must be furnished by 30 ___.

questions.concept: Change in control: branch vs incorporated
questions.question: An IFSC-incorporated CMI may complete a change in control and then intimate the Authority within 15 days.
questions.explanation: Reg 23(2): an incorporated CMI needs PRIOR approval. The 15-day intimation route is for a branch under Reg 23(1).

questions.concept: Change in control: branch vs incorporated
questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes the two change-in-control routes?
questions.option_A: Both require prior approval
questions.option_B: Both are satisfied by intimation within 15 days
questions.option_C: A branch intimates within 15 days after; an IFSC-incorporated CMI must obtain prior approval before
questions.option_D: The route depends on deal size, not legal form
questions.correct_text: A branch intimates within 15 days after; an IFSC-incorporated CMI must obtain prior approval before
questions.explanation: Reg 23(1) and 23(2). The distinction turns entirely on legal form.

questions.question: Which is NOT expressly required by Chapter III?
questions.option_A: A business continuity plan reviewed annually
questions.option_B: A cyber security and resilience framework
questions.option_C: A quarterly statement of net worth
questions.option_D: A minimum staff headcount in the IFSC
questions.correct_text: A minimum staff headcount in the IFSC
questions.explanation: Reg 20, 21 and 16(1)(d) impose the other three. Chapter III sets no headcount minimum.

questions.question: Failing to co-operate with an inspection is itself a ground for suspension or cancellation.
questions.explanation: Reg 41(1)(f) — independent of the underlying issue.

questions.question: A relaxation application under Reg 44 is processed within ___ days of a complete application.
questions.explanation: Reg 44 — accompanied by a non-refundable fee.

questions.question: Which is NOT a Reg 41 ground for action?
questions.option_A: Reporting a loss for two consecutive financial years
questions.option_B: Furnishing false or misleading information in a material particular
questions.option_C: Failing to resolve investor complaints
questions.option_D: Non-cooperation in an inspection
questions.correct_text: Reporting a loss for two consecutive financial years
questions.explanation: Reg 41(1)(d), (g) and (f) cover the others. Trading losses are not, of themselves, a listed ground.

questions.question: The Authority must always give notice before inspecting a CMI.
questions.explanation: Reg 37(3): notice is the norm, but may be dispensed with for reasons recorded in writing where investors' interest requires.

questions.question: A clearing member needs a fresh certificate of registration to act as a broker dealer.
questions.explanation: Reg 5(4)(a): with the exchange's approval and WITHOUT a separate certificate.

questions.question: Broker-dealer net worth is …
questions.option_B: as specified by the recognised stock exchange
questions.option_D: as specified by the depository
questions.correct_text: as specified by the recognised stock exchange
questions.explanation: Schedule I, S.No. 1 — and measured on liquid assets per Reg 3(1)(cc).

questions.question: A CRA may withdraw a rating at the issuer's request while the rated obligations remain outstanding.
questions.explanation: Reg 28(5): generally no withdrawal while obligations are outstanding, save specified situations. A bare request is not one.

questions.question: A custodian may share books and access with the group's proprietary trading desk if reconciliations are performed.
questions.explanation: Reg 29(1) requires custody to be separated and segregated from ALL other activities.

questions.concept: Debenture trustee: independence, reporting, nominee director
questions.question: A debenture trustee appoints a nominee director on ___ consecutive interest defaults.
questions.explanation: Reg 30(3)(f) — or on default in security creation or redemption.

questions.concept: Debenture trustee: independence, reporting, nominee director
questions.question: DT periodic reports: within 7 days of the board meeting or ___ days of the quarter, whichever is earlier.
A depository participant may reconcile with the depository weekly.
questions.explanation: Reg 31(5): reconciliation is a DAILY obligation.

questions.question: Which is NOT permitted for a depository participant?
questions.option_A: Opening a separate account for each beneficial owner
questions.option_B: Reconciling with the depository at each day's close
questions.option_C: Holding a buffer of client securities in its own proprietary account
questions.option_D: Maintaining data-processing integrity
questions.correct_text: Holding a buffer of client securities in its own proprietary account
questions.explanation: Reg 31(2) forbids mixing beneficial owners' securities with the participant's own.

An ERDPP must comply strictly with its code of conduct, with no explain option.
questions.explanation: Reg 33(3): the ERDPP code applies on a 'comply or explain' basis, with disclosure of compliance.

questions.question: An investment adviser may accept a trail commission from a fund house whose scheme it recommends.
questions.explanation: Reg 34(4): no consideration from any person other than the client advised, in respect of the underlying products.

questions.question: An adviser must not trade on own account contrary to its advice for ___ days.
questions.explanation: Reg 34(6), subject to the 24-hour revised-assessment exception.

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes an investment adviser from a distributor?
questions.option_A: Both may accept product-provider remuneration
questions.option_B: Neither may charge the client directly
questions.option_C: The difference is only the net worth figure
questions.option_D: An adviser may be paid only by the client advised; a distributor may be product-remunerated
questions.correct_text: An adviser may be paid only by the client advised; a distributor may be product-remunerated
questions.explanation: Reg 34(4) is the bright line. A distributor's Part B code instead targets mis-selling and prohibits attracting clients by rebate.

questions.question: An investment banker that promotes the issuer may act as book-running lead manager if it discloses the relationship.
questions.explanation: Reg 35(3): a promoter or associate of the issuer may undertake NO activity except marketing of the issue.

questions.question: A registered investment adviser issuing public research must separately register as a research entity.
questions.explanation: Reg 4(4): a registered IA, CRA or FME issuing research to the public need not separately register.

questions.question: A standalone firm that only publishes public research and holds no other IFSCA registration must …
questions.option_A: register as a research entity
questions.option_B: rely on the Reg 4(4) exemption
questions.option_C: register as a credit rating agency
questions.option_D: do nothing
questions.correct_text: register as a research entity
questions.explanation: The Reg 4(4) exemption is confined to entities already registered as IA, CRA or FME.

questions.question: Which obligation is COMMON to every CMI?
questions.option_A: Daily reconciliation with the depository
questions.option_B: Preserving records for eight years
questions.option_C: Appointing a nominee director on default
questions.option_D: Segregating custody from other activities
questions.correct_text: Preserving records for eight years
questions.explanation: Reg 16 binds all CMIs. The others are DP, DT and custodian specific.

questions.option_A: The Schedule II Part A code of conduct
questions.option_B: The annual compliance audit by 30 September
questions.option_C: The 15-day own-account restriction after giving advice
questions.option_D: Change-in-control obligations
questions.correct_text: The 15-day own-account restriction after giving advice
questions.explanation: Reg 34(6) binds investment advisers only. The others bind every CMI.
